_readme: THE OPERATIONS REGISTER — [pipeline O-1] Private/requirements/ (was pipeline/14-operations.md, folded into the JSON spec 2026-08-15)
Every failure this factory can suffer, every recurring duty it performs, every surface it serves,
every revert path, every recovery drill, every expiring thing and every retention obligation — each
with a detector, a response, an owner, a cadence and a date. One person cannot hold this; a file can.
WHY IT EXISTS, AND WHY IT IS THE SIXTH REGISTER RATHER THAN A SECTION OF ONE OF THE OTHER FIVE.
Eighteen of stage 14's twenty-one acceptance criteria quantify over 'the operations register'. Until
this file landed that set did not exist (`ls tooling/ops` -> No such file or directory), so all
eighteen ranged over nothing and reported clean. An undefined right-hand side cannot reject anything.
The other five registers answer different questions and are read by other stages' guards:
tooling/capability-register.json  — what shared capability exists and who consumes it   [2]/[3]
tooling/channel-register.json     — what channel is SERVED and with which identity      [9]/[10]
tooling/screen-register.json      — which non-app-specific screens ship in the chassis   [2]/[5]
tooling/platform-register.json    — the shared server's routes and bindings              [4]
tooling/dod-register.json         — the definition of done, per app                      [6]
tooling/monitor-register.json     — every HOSTNAME served, and whether anything watches it [11]
tooling/ceilings.json             — the sourced free-tier ceilings the budgets derive from [4]
Merging this one into any of them would put four other stages' guards on the same file.
🔴 AND THIS REGISTER HOLDS NO HOSTNAMES, ON PURPOSE — THE ONE PLACE IT NEARLY BECAME A SECOND
SOURCE OF TRUTH. Its first draft carried six `surface` rows, one per live hostname, each restating
which GlitchTip monitor watches it and which two are unwatched. [11]E-9's monitor-register.json had
landed the same day with the same facts and a WIDER derivation (Worker custom domains ∪ the app
catalogue ∪ every site's canonical URL, against custom domains alone here) — and its own header says
"[14]O-2 must CONSUME this register rather than re-enumerate the hostnames". Two registers of one set
drift the first time a canonical URL moves and nobody edits both. The rows were CUT and
`_delegated.hostnames` replaces them: assert-ops-register.mjs refuses to run if that file is absent,
unparseable, empty, or blind to a custom domain this repo deploys. Delegation that cannot fail is
just an absence with better manners.
WHY THE PUBLIC REPO AND NOT Private/. CI cannot read Private/ — it is gitignored and invisible to
every workflow, which is exactly what blocked four stage-8 increments. This file holds surface names,
cadences and dates. No credential, no business identifier, no PII. The private CONTENT (the runbooks
themselves) stays in Private/, the owner queue in nikatru/; the STRUCTURAL FACTS a guard reads live here.
Enforced by tooling/ci/assert-ops-register.mjs (schema, coverage, staleness, revert mitigations,
access-path intersection) and tooling/ci/assert-retention-coverage.mjs (the `retention` rows against
the stores actually enumerated from the tree).
`kind`      one of the eight in `_kinds`. Free text here would let a row opt out of every per-kind
rule below by inventing a ninth kind nothing checks.
`cadence`   a duration (`8h`, `1d`, `7d`, `120d`), OR `on-demand` — WHICH REQUIRES A NON-EMPTY
`why` — OR `trigger`, which requires a named `trigger` event. Three kinds, because the
first draft had only the first two and the parked fresh-host drill fits neither: it is
not on a clock and it is not on-demand, it fires when the next Windows machine is set up.
EVERY duration IS BOUNDED BY `_maxCadenceDays` PER KIND, so a row cannot declare its own
ten-year shelf life and pass. `on-demand` is the escape hatch this stage's audit found in
eighteen criteria; the `why` and the printed count are what stop it being free.
`lastDone`  ⚠️ REQUIRED ONLY FOR THE KINDS A HUMAN PERFORMS — `recovery-path`, `revert`, `review`,
`lastDrill` `failure-mode`. THIS IS A DELIBERATE DEVIATION from the drafted 'absent is a failure for
every kind'. A hand-typed `lastDone` on a nightly cron is a date nobody updates: it would
be written once, go stale in a day, and then either fail CI forever or be bumped by hand
in every unrelated commit — which is the 'record that records success unconditionally'
this stage exists to eliminate, wearing a register's clothes. A MACHINE duty must instead
declare `mechanism.record` + `mechanism.failingValue` — a place a reader can go and a
value that reader can find there and go red on. Duties therefore satisfy an XOR: a human
date, or a machine record whose failing value is reachable. Neither is optional.
`mechanism` `.substrate` names WHAT runs it, `.anchor` a repo-relative path THAT MUST EXIST (a
mechanism naming a file that is gone is a mechanism that is gone), `.record` where its
run history is readable, `.failingValue` the value in that record that means FAILED, and
`.readBy` the thing that actually looks. `grep -rn cron_heartbeat` returning zero readers
while the table carried three consecutive red nights is why `.readBy` is a field.
`accessProviders` resolved from `_providers`, NEVER free text. This is the whole of what makes O-14
computable: a `failure-mode` row names the providers it TAKES DOWN, and the recovery row
it points at names the providers it NEEDS — two independently written lists, and the
guard intersects them. The drafted version compared two sets written by the same hand in
the same row, so a row declaring an empty dependency set could never intersect anything.
`source`    `verified` (measured or read from the thing itself) or `unverified` (corroborated only
by secondary sources — the OCI 30-day abandonment clause, the two statutory breach
clocks). The unverified count PRINTS on every run. Never restate an unverified number as
a fact somewhere else in the repo on the strength of its being written down here.
`ownerGated` the row's missing half can only be supplied from a vendor console, a laptop, or the
proprietor's own knowledge. The guard PRINTS these on every run and does not block —
CLAUDE.md's C-6 rule: a guard that blocks all of CI on work only the owner can do gets
disabled, and a disabled guard checks nothing. It is not a waiver: the gap is counted and
named in every single log line, and rows carrying a DATED tripwire fail after that date.
── THREE THINGS THAT ARE SETTLED AND MUST NOT BE RE-LITIGATED HERE ────────────────────────────────
· [ADR 021] backup destination + the deliberate REMOVAL of encryption.
· [ADR 022] pack-signing key custody — paper + .claude/, Shamir NOT required.
· OWNER_QUEUE S-1 — the GitHub PAT stays broad-scoped and never-expiring, deliberately. It is
referenced by no workflow, so it contributes NO `expiring` row at all: out of the domain by
fact, not by policy. Do not add one, and do not add a rotation reminder.

_why: [14]O-7. A deployable surface must be PROBED after it ships, in the job that shipped it — the domain is
derived from `record-deployment.mjs` calls plus every directory under sites/, so deleting a deploy job
cannot be the way to satisfy the check. These two surfaces have no deploy job to add a step to, and that
is a decision rather than an omission: [F-9] rejected migrating the Cloudflare Git-integration sites into
Actions. Their coverage is O-2's external prober, named here so a NEW site arrives unclassified and red
rather than unwatched and quiet.
📌 APPENDED 2026-08-26 — A THIRD ENTRY ARRIVED AND IT IS NOT THE SAME SHAPE AS THE FIRST TWO. The two
above are exempt because there is NO JOB to probe from. `subscriptiontracker-linux-snap` HAS a job; it is exempt
because the surface carries nothing a probe could JOIN ON. The distinction decides the next entry:
"no job" is a fact about this repository and is retired by a workflow, "nothing joinable" is a fact
about a vendor and is retired by a URL. The Play lane was examined in the same pass and came out the
OTHER WAY — it has a job AND a joinable read, so it got a real smoke and NOT an entry here.
📌 APPENDED 2026-08-26 — A FOURTH ENTRY WAS CONSIDERED FOR `build-platforms.yml:release` AND IS DELIBERATELY
NOT HERE. That job records `$environment` and entered this limb's domain only today, when the shared workflow
reader learned to match a QUOTED SHELL VARIABLE; before that it was dropped in silence and the census printed
"7 deploy job(s)" without it. It got a REAL PROBE rather than an entry, and on the Play test rather than the
Snap one: the GitHub API reports every release asset's `digest` as `sha256:<hex>`, MEASURED 2026-08-26 against
a real release (cli/cli v2.92.0, the API digest re-checked with `sha256sum` over the downloaded asset) to be
exactly the sha256 of the bytes the release serves — and dist/SHA256SUMS already carries that number for every
asset this job staged. So the read joins on what THIS RUN PRODUCED, in both directions, and NOT on "a release
exists at this tag", which a release published last month answers just as well. Snap's three grounds all fail
here: the digest is a machine-readable join key, no reviewer stands between `gh release create` and the read,
and the transport is the same REST API the publish already speaks. The probe is the step named "The release
must carry the assets this job just uploaded" in .github/workflows/build-platforms.yml.
_deploySmokeExemptions.site:nikatru: Deployed by Cloudflare Git integration, not by a workflow — there is no job to probe from. Covered by O-2's external prober (tooling/ops/status.mjs) against the hostname enumerated in tooling/monitor-register.json, which is stage 11's derivation and strictly wider than anything this file would restate. ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-11. This line read '⚠️ THREE of that register's monitors are still `Ping` rather than `GET`+expectedStatus — nikatru.com (id 4), rajasekarselvam.com (id 5) and Subly web (id 3) — and a Pages project serving a 500 or a blank shell answers a ping … OWNER_QUEUE S-8.' All three were converted on the live instance with the vault GLITCHTIP_TOKEN and one PUT each; tooling/ops/status.mjs now probes 7 of 7 declared hostnames and prints `0 of 7 … are unprobeable`. 🔴 IT WAS NEVER OWNER WORK — the same wrong filing tooling/monitor-register.json records for the two monitors it CREATED on 2026-08-05, repeated on the conversion. ✅ AND THE RESIDUAL IS CLOSED FOR THE TWO HTML SITES, 2026-08-11: monitors 4 and 5 now assert an `expectedBody` — each site's own canonical link tag, which is host-specific and is absent from the 404 these Pages projects serve, so a blank shell or an edge error page no longer passes. Deleting or retargeting that tag also fails the build, because tooling/ci/assert-monitor-coverage.mjs derives the hostname from it; a mere REFORMAT of it does not, because that guard's regex tolerates whitespace and single quotes while the monitor's match is exact. Monitor 3 (Subly web) asserts the built shell's base-href tag, which proves the served bytes are a real flutter build web output and NOT that the app booted: a monitor runs no JavaScript, so that half stays with the nightly e2e. The count in this file was also wrong twice (`Two` until 2026-08-09 against a register carrying three), which is why the number belongs to the printed count and not to this sentence. ⏱ 2026-09-07 — APPENDED, NOT REWRITTEN, AND THE SENTENCE IT CORRECTS IS THE ONE ABOVE READING 'tooling/ops/status.mjs now probes 7 of 7 declared hostnames and prints `0 of 7 … are unprobeable`'. It was true on 2026-08-11. BOTH HALVES ARE FALSE NOW, and the pager-monitors unit (ADR 067) is what made them false. Re-measured today: `node tooling/ops/status.mjs` (exit 0) prints 'probing 9 surface(s)' and '2 of 11 declared hostname(s) CANNOT BE PROBED', and `node tooling/ci/assert-monitor-coverage.mjs` (exit 0) prints `11 declared, 9 monitored, 2 gap(s)`. FOUR Box B rows landed in tooling/monitor-register.json: ntfy.nikatru.com and vault.nikatru.com, each with a real GlitchTip monitor (ids 31, 32) against a health endpoint whose body is asserted, and beszel.nikatru.com and logs.nikatru.com, both behind Cloudflare Access, where the 302 a prober sees is produced at the EDGE before the origin is consulted — so each carries `monitor: null` and a stated gap that this file, assert-monitor-coverage and verify-monitors all print on every run, rather than a GET+302 monitor that would have read 11 of 11 while watching Cloudflare. COVERAGE WENT UP — 7 of 7 declared to 9 of 11 declared — and the shortfall is louder, not quieter. The closing sentence of this same paragraph, 'which is why the number belongs to the printed count and not to this sentence', is its own rule, and this is the THIRD time this sentence has broken it (`Two` until 2026-08-09, then `7 of 7` until today). No guard grades this prose, so it is corrected by a dated measurement set beside the frozen wording instead of by editing it — and the rule stands: read the printed count, never this sentence. ⏱ APPENDED 2026-09-09 — THE COVERAGE CLAIM ABOVE IS NOW STRICTLY STRONGER, and the sentence it strengthens was the weak half. O-2's external prober answers "is the hostname serving something we recognise RIGHT NOW"; it cannot answer "did Cloudflare's build for the newest commit on main ever land", and those are different questions with the same green. A project stuck on a three-week-old commit passes the prober on every slot. duty.pages-deployment-landed (tooling/ops/check-pages-deployments.mjs, the pages-deployments job in ops-watch.yml) now grades latest_stage.status against deployment_trigger.metadata.commit_hash for exactly this project, so the Git-integration build finally has an observer of its own. The exemption is KEPT rather than deleted: there is still no deploy job here to add a post-deploy smoke step to, which is what this entry is an exemption FROM.

_deploySmokeExemptions.subscriptiontracker-linux-snap: 🔴 NOT "stores are slow" — a SPECIFIC surface carries nothing a probe can join on, for three separate reasons, and closing ANY ONE of them retires this entry. (1) THERE IS NO JOIN KEY. `snapcraft upload` documents no machine-readable output, and the REVISION ID is recorded UNSOURCED in tooling/release/submit-snap.mjs (UNSOURCED[0]): `manageRevisions` says a number "can be obtained with the `snapcraft revisions` command", whose output FORMAT is documented on no page fetched. The only value a probe could compare is the snap VERSION — and a version is NOT unique across revisions, so a channel already carrying an earlier revision of the same version answers such a probe correctly while THIS upload shipped nothing. That is green over precisely the failure it exists to catch: the `Ping` finding tooling/monitor-register.json records, repeated on a store. (2) A NEGATIVE READ IS NOT EVIDENCE EITHER, SO THE PROBE CANNOT EVEN FAIL HONESTLY. `--release` takes effect only "if the store review passes"; that review is AUTOMATIC and happens ON UPLOAD; and `need_manual_review` is an enumerated status. So a channel map that does not yet name this upload is a documented, expected state of a GOOD submission, and failing on it would be a false red on the honest path — the 2026-08-04 lesson tooling/ops/post-deploy-smoke.mjs carries in its own header. (3) THERE IS NO TRANSPORT TO READ FROM. Everything this repo sends to the store goes through `snapcraft`, because UNSOURCED[1] records that the mapping from SNAPCRAFT_STORE_CREDENTIALS onto the store API’s `Authorization: Macaroon root=…, discharge=…` header is not sourced — no request in this tree reaches dashboard.snapcraft.io. And `snapcraft whoami`’s output is ALREADY refused as a parse target in that same file because its format is undocumented; parsing `snapcraft status` would break that rule one command over. 🔴 WHAT COVERS IT INSTEAD: NOTHING DOES, AND THAT IS WRITTEN DOWN AS A GAP RATHER THAN DRESSED AS COVERAGE. The two site: entries above delegate to O-2’s external prober; this one delegates to nobody. The [10]D-9 row this job writes says `in_review` and claims only "we submitted"; the transition to `live` is a separate act nothing in this repository performs. The row is also `served: false` in tooling/channel-register.json and the job has never run, so the gap is real but not yet load-bearing — which is the moment to write it down, not the moment to forget it. WHAT RETIRES THIS ENTRY, and it is one fact either way: a SOURCED machine-readable revision id (UNSOURCED[0]) or the macaroon header mapping (UNSOURCED[1]). Either makes a read-after-upload joinable, and tooling/ops/post-deploy-smoke.mjs then gets a snap limb the way it got a Play one on 2026-08-26. ⚠️ DO NOT COPY THIS ONTO THE PLAY LANE — it was checked on 2026-08-26 and came out the OTHER WAY. .github/workflows/submit-play.yml:submit now runs a real post-deploy smoke, because androidpublisher’s `edits.tracks.list` returns the versionCodes each track carries and the versionCode IS a machine-readable key the upload produces. "The store has a review queue" is true of BOTH channels and settles NEITHER: it is an argument about the LISTING, and the Play probe does not read the listing.
_deploySmokeExemptions.subscriptiontracker-windows-store: 🔴 THE SAME SHAPE AS subscriptiontracker-linux-snap, AND FOR A DIFFERENT REASON EACH TIME — so it is written out rather than pointed at that entry. Recorded 2026-09-07, when submit-windows-store.yml grew a `submit` job that records `subscriptiontracker-windows-store --state in_review`. (1) THE SUBMISSION IS NOT THE LISTING, AND ONLY THE LISTING IS PROBEABLE. learn.microsoft.com "Manage app submissions" (fetched 2026-09-07) says a committed submission moves `CommitStarted → PreProcessing`, and everything after PreProcessing is Microsoft's certification queue — so at the moment this job ends, nothing is live at apps.microsoft.com and a probe of the storefront would be reading the PREVIOUS version, or a 404 on a first submission. A green probe there would mean "the old build is still up", which is the exact false comfort tooling/ops/post-deploy-smoke.mjs's own header records from 2026-08-04. (2) THE ONLY READ-AFTER-WRITE THAT WOULD MEAN ANYTHING IS THE SUBMISSION STATUS, AND THE LANE ALREADY MAKES IT: `msstore submission poll` is the fourth call the script runs, and it is what turns a `CommitFailed` into a non-zero exit before this record is written at all — the record step carries `if: always() && steps.submit.outcome == 'success'`. So the read exists; it is not a `post-deploy-smoke.mjs` step and it cannot become one, because the value it reads is a submission id inside Partner Center rather than a public surface a prober can reach without the four MS_STORE_* credentials. (3) THE JOB HAS NEVER RUN AND CANNOT RUN YET. The Partner Center account has no Entra tenant, so `msstore reconfigure` has nothing to authenticate against, and `served: false` in tooling/channel-register.json still holds for this row. The gap is real and not yet load-bearing, which is the moment to write it down rather than the moment to forget it. 🔴 WHAT RETIRES THIS ENTRY: a first real submission that yields a PUBLIC join key — the storefront URL for the product id, once one listing exists — at which point post-deploy-smoke.mjs can assert that apps.microsoft.com serves that product at the version this run submitted, the way the Play lane got a real smoke on 2026-08-26 off `edits.tracks.list`'s versionCodes. Until a first listing exists there is nothing on the public internet to join on. ⚠️ DO NOT READ THIS AS "stores are slow": the Play lane was checked on 2026-08-26 and came out the OTHER WAY.

_why: One set, one owner. `hostnames` is [11]E-9's: tooling/monitor-register.json enumerates every host
this factory serves and whether a monitor watches it, derived from the tree by
tooling/ci/assert-monitor-coverage.mjs on every run. This register names the delegate rather than
restating its rows, and its guard fails if the delegate is missing, unparseable, empty, or blind to
a custom domain this repo deploys — so "stage 11 owns it" stays a fact instead of becoming nobody's.
[14]O-4 — WHICH MACHINE IS THIS THING ON. Every `duty` row names the substrate that RUNS it and,
if it is on a clock, an `absenceWatcher` naming the substrate that notices when it STOPS. The
criterion is that the watcher is on DIFFERENT INFRASTRUCTURE, and this map is what makes that a
comparison between two machines instead of between two spellings.
🔴 THE CASE THAT FORCED IT. `oci-cron` and `glitchtip-heartbeat` are different words for THE SAME
ORACLE BOX. The four crontab duties on that host are watched by a GlitchTip instance running on
that host, so the machine failure that silences them silences the watcher AND the mail that would
say so, in the same instant — and the result is indistinguishable from perfect health. A string
comparison would have called that 'different infrastructure' and printed ok. Resolving both sides
to a HOST makes it fail, which is the only reason the limb is worth having.
Every value is a member of `_providers` — the same fixed vocabulary O-14's intersection resolves
against — because free text on the right-hand side is how a comparison stops comparing. A
substrate with no entry here FAILS as 'cannot be checked' rather than passing, and an entry no row
reaches is DELETED rather than kept: a mapping about nothing inflates the domain while resolving
nothing.
⚠️ `renovate-app` resolves to `github` deliberately, and it USED TO BE the one judgement call in
this map. It no longer is: the Mend-hosted App was UNINSTALLED on 2026-09-03 and Renovate now runs
from .github/workflows/renovate.yml, so the duty runs on GitHub Actions and its RECORD (the
Dependency Dashboard issue, the `chore/renovate-*` branches) lives on GitHub too. The mapping is
unchanged and the REASON for it is not: it was a judgement about a third-party host whose record
happened to live here, and it is now simply where the thing runs.
🔴 THE SUBSTRATE NAME IS KEPT ON PURPOSE, not out of inertia. `duty.renovate` is about the BOT
proposing updates; `duty.workflow.renovate.yml` is about the WORKFLOW firing. They fail
independently — the workflow can run green every day while the bot proposes nothing — so renaming
this substrate to `github-actions` would read as one duty where there are two. The map answers
'where would a watcher have to look', which is the question the criterion is about, and both
answers are still `github`.
_portabilityWhy: 🔴 A SUBSTRATE NAMES A ROLE, NEVER A BOX — CHANGED 2026-09-03, AND THE COST OF LEARNING THAT WAS 46
HOURS OF FROZEN DEPLOYMENTS. `oci-cron` and `glitchtip-heartbeat` both resolved to `oci`. GlitchTip
and its whole backup chain moved to the Hostinger box on 2026-09-02, and BOTH mappings silently
became false: measured on 2026-09-03, all four `/opt/glitchtip/*` crons run on Box B (02:00, 02:30,
:41, :17 — matched against the live crontab, not inferred), and GlitchTip itself serves from Box B.
⚠️ THE STALENESS INVERTED A SAFETY CHECK RATHER THAN JUST AGEING. [14]O-4 asks whether a duty's
WATCHER is on different infrastructure from the duty. With both sides pinned to `oci` it kept
reporting the Oracle-box SPOF after the duties had left that box — a true-sounding finding about a
machine that no longer ran them. A map that is wrong in this direction is worse than absent: it
➡️ THE PROPERTY THIS BUYS, AND IT IS THE WHOLE POINT WITH LIVE USERS: moving a service to another
box is now ONE edit — the host on the right-hand side here. Nothing else in the register, and
nothing in tooling/ops/alarm-chains.json (which keys monitors by `id` since 2026-09-03), needs to
change. Before this, a move required at least four scattered edits and missing any one froze every
merge and both deploys 36 HOURS LATER, with nothing in the failure naming the move.
⛔ NEVER put a box name in a substrate, a monitor name, or a row id. `glitchtip-box-cron` says WHICH
SERVICE'S box; the answer to WHICH MACHINE lives here and only here.
_selfhostBackupCronWhy: ⚠️ A SECOND CRON SUBSTRATE ON THE SAME HOST, ADDED 2026-09-05, AND IT IS NOT A DUPLICATE OF
`glitchtip-box-cron`. Both resolve to `hostinger` today and they are still two different roles:
`glitchtip-box-cron` is the crontab of the box that RUNS GLITCHTIP (the 02:00 dump, the 02:30 Drive
sync, the :41 liveness check, the :17 disk alert, and the 02:45 Cloudflare pull, all of them
`/opt/glitchtip/*` scripts); `selfhost-backup-cron` is the crontab of the box that HOLDS THE RESTIC
🔴 THE REASON IS THE ONE THIS MAP EXISTS FOR — a substrate names a ROLE, never a box. Folding restic
into `glitchtip-box-cron` would work exactly until GlitchTip moved and somebody edited that one
right-hand side: the restic rows would silently follow GlitchTip to a machine that does not hold their
repositories, and [14]O-4 would go on answering confidently about the wrong box. That is the failure
`_portabilityWhy` above records costing 46 hours of frozen deployments, in the direction where it is
hardest to notice, because both spellings would still resolve to a real host.
The cost of the split is one extra line here on the day the backups move, and the map's own rule that
an entry no row reaches is DELETED keeps it from becoming clutter: this key is reached by
_supabaseBoxCronWhy: 🔴 A THIRD CRON SUBSTRATE, ADDED 2026-09-06, AND UNTIL THAT DAY THIS MAP HAD NO ENTRY FOR THE ONE BOX
THE PRODUCT CANNOT SURVIVE LOSING. `sudo crontab -l` on the auth box has held five root jobs since
2026-09-02 and NOT ONE of them had a row in this register: measured 2026-09-03 and again on 2026-09-06,
zero rows mentioned `/opt/supabase`. The consequence was the opposite of convenient — a Box A move had
no declaration to update BECAUSE IT HAD NONE, so the crons would have travelled silently and nothing
here would have noticed any of them failing to come back.
⚠️ AND THE IDS ALREADY IN THIS FILE ACTIVELY MISLEAD ON THAT POINT. The five `duty.oci.*` rows read as
though they cover the Oracle box; every one of them describes an `/opt/glitchtip/*` script on the
SERVICES box. A reader scanning ids would have concluded the auth box was covered. It was not. The new
rows are named for their ROLE (`duty.supabase-*`) precisely so the next reader cannot make that
inference from a name, which is what `_portabilityWhy` above has been asking for since 2026-09-03.
⚠️ TWO SCRIPTS SHARE A NAME ACROSS THE TWO BOXES AND THE COLLISION IS THE TRAP. BOTH boxes run a
`disk-alert.py` hourly at :17 and BOTH run a `backup-liveness.py`. `duty.oci.disk-alert` and
`duty.oci.backup-liveness` are the SERVICES box's; `duty.supabase-disk-alert` and
`duty.supabase-backup-liveness` are this one's. Do not assume a row about "the disk alert" is about the
machine you have in mind.
🔴 AND THE :17 IS NOT THE SAME INSTANT ON THE TWO BOXES. The services box runs Etc/UTC; the auth box
runs Asia/Kolkata (+0530), measured with `timedatectl` on 2026-09-06. So its `17 * * * *` fires at :47
UTC and its `47 * * * *` at :17 UTC — which is exactly where monitor 19's hourly checks have been
landing since 2026-09-02, and is the arithmetic that corrects Private/runbooks/boxes/oracle.md's cron
table from a UTC heading to an IST one.
This key is reached by the five `duty.supabase-*` rows and by nothing else. It resolves to `oci` today;
the whole point of the map is that a move is this one right-hand side and nothing else.

_why: A stage-level ceiling per kind, so a row cannot buy itself an unreachable shelf life. These are
JUDGEMENT CALLS AND ARE RECORDED AS SUCH — none is a vendor SLA and none may be cited as one.
Each is set at the point where 'we last checked' stops being a useful sentence for that kind of
thing, and each is one number, changed deliberately.

absenceWatcher.margin: MISSED_RUN_GRACE_HOURS = 2, anchored on the OCCURRENCE: the reader takes the most recent time the cron was DUE and asks whether a row exists at or after it, allowing 2 h for a late one. 🔴 THE SENTENCE THIS REPLACES DESCRIBED A MECHANISM check-heartbeats.mjs DELETED ON 2026-08-06, AND IT SURVIVED HERE FOR A MONTH. It read: '1.5x the 24h cron interval = a 36h ceiling before absence alarms. One missed run is not an alarm; two are. The ratio is the backup chain's own and is written down once, in check-heartbeats.mjs.' Every clause of that is now false. The ratio is not in that file; the ceiling is not 36 h; and the rule it stated was never what 1.5x bought in the first place - at age 2C two runs have been missed, so a 1.5C window fires on the FIRST miss, not the second. This row's OWN `downTransitionDrill.scope` already said 'the occurrence-anchored ABSENCE limb' while these two fields went on describing the ratio, which is the shape a stale claim takes: one field learns and its neighbours do not. WHY THE OCCURRENCE AND NOT A BIGGER RATIO, in check-heartbeats.mjs's own words and its own measurement: a ratio is measured from the LAST SUCCESS, so it drifts with whatever time the previous run happened to land, and it answers 'how stale is the newest row' when the question is 'did the run that was supposed to happen, happen'. So on the Actions page — the page a human actually reads — a Cloudflare build that FAILED is indistinguishable from one that was never needed, and a project stuck on a three-week-old commit looks exactly like a quiet week. Measured precedent: on 2026-08-19 all 25 production deployments of the `nikatru` project were sitting at `queued`/`idle` and nothing in this repository could have said so. 🔴 AND THAT PROJECT IS NOT A MARKETING SITE ANY MORE — since ADR 075 the apex is the app's PUBLIC ADDRESS and sites/nikatru/functions/_middleware.js is the ROUTER that proxies nikatru.com/<id>/ to the app's own Pages project. A stuck router therefore serves 404s at the app's address while deploy-web.yml, the app's own Pages project and the post-deploy smoke are all three green — the white-page failure mode with the whole deploy lane reporting success.
rows.detector: tooling/ops/check-pages-deployments.mjs, run by .github/workflows/ops-watch.yml in its own `pages-deployments` job (which needs `fetch-depth: 0`, because the freshness limb asks `git log -1 origin/main -- sites/<name>`). It reads GET /accounts/{account}/pages/projects/{project}/deployments?env=production for a project set DERIVED from sites/* (minus _shared) and catalog/apps.json, and grades two things: `latest_stage.name === 'deploy' && latest_stage.status === 'success'`, and — for git-connected projects only — `deployment_trigger.metadata.commit_hash` against the newest commit on main touching that project's source directory. Direct-upload projects carry `deployment_trigger.type: ad_hoc` and no commit_hash, so their commit limb is declared UNGRADED and COUNTED rather than skipped; their commit witness is record-deployment.mjs on the pipeline B-17 rail. Three-valued: 0 every project landed at the commit main names · 1 a project is red, or succeeded at a stale commit · 2 COULD NOT LOOK (no credential, a non-200, unparseable JSON, a preview row returned for a production query, or a project set that derived to EMPTY).
rows.response: Exit 1 fails the pages-deployments job, which reaches the durable ops-watch issue. The repair is a Cloudflare-side retry of the failed build, or the cause of its failure; it is NEVER a change to this reader, because the surface really is serving older bytes than main. Exit 2 is the separate "nothing was judged" state and fails too — an empty sweep prints the same ok as a complete one, and this is the one rail with no second witness to fall back on.

remotelessHistoryLimb.what: Two changes in `.claude\scripts\backup-offsite.ps1`, made together because either alone is half a fix. (1) ORDERING: the `git bundles` job is PREPENDED to the job list instead of appended, so it runs FIRST and no plain-file mirror can fail in front of it. (2) ASSERTION: for every repo in the bundle list that has NO git remote, every LOCAL TAG must be present in the bundle this run just wrote, and the remote file must be byte-for-byte that bundle — size AND md5, read back from the provider. Absent, stale, tagless, hashless and unreadable are all FAILURES; 'I could not tell' never reads as 'it is fine'.
remotelessHistoryLimb.failsHow: It throws inside the copy loop, before the heartbeat POST — so the consequence is this duty's EXISTING alarm chain, not a new one that would need its own drill. A remoteless repo whose only off-machine history did not arrive takes monitor 6 Down and mails support@nikatru.com, the path the 2026-08-05 down-transition drill below proved end to end.

provenBites.negativeTest: .claude\scripts\test\remoteless-history.negative.ps1, reachable as `backup-offsite.ps1 -SelfTest`. All three are caught, and the suite FAILS if any of them ever stops being caught.
provenBites.liveGreen: Run against the real machine and the real Drive: 2 remoteless repos (the private corpus, 2 tags; the business brain, 1 tag), every local tag present in its bundle, remote md5 identical to local for both. Checked=2, failures=0.
provenBites.liveRed: Same code against a genuinely tagless bundle built with `git bundle create --branches`: 'REMOTELESS repo has 2 tag(s) in NO bundle - pre-minimal-2026-09-08, pre-prune-2026-09-08'. That is 2026-09-08's actual Drive state, reproduced and caught.
provenBites.harnessDefectFound: 🔴 THE FIRST HARNESS WAS ITSELF THE BUG, AND IT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY FIXED. It dot-sourced the extracted block into a helper function's scope, so the second run silently re-executed the FIRST run's definition and every mutation reported 'behaved IDENTICALLY' — the harness declaring the guard worthless when in fact the harness had not re-read it. Same class as the defect this register keeps finding: a check that returns a verdict about code it did not run.

rows.path: workflow_dispatch on deploy-workers.yml against the last green SHA 📌 CORRECTED 2026-08-25 — APPENDED, NOTHING ABOVE REWRITTEN. AS WRITTEN, THE DISPATCH-AGAINST-A-SHA HALF OF THIS PATH IS NOT EXECUTABLE. Measured this run: `grep -n "inputs:" .github/workflows/deploy-web.yml .github/workflows/deploy-workers.yml` returns NOTHING — neither workflow declares a single workflow_dispatch input (deploy-workers.yml:26 and deploy-web.yml:29 are bare `workflow_dispatch:` keys — deploy-workers re-measured 2026-09-06 after its prose moved to docs/ci/deploy-workers.md; the :21 it said before landed on a comment line), and GitHub's 'Run workflow' ref picker offers BRANCHES AND TAGS ONLY, never a bare commit SHA. So there has never been a control anywhere that accepts the SHA this sentence tells the operator to type. WHAT IS ACTUALLY EXECUTABLE: cut a branch at the target SHA and dispatch against THAT BRANCH — `git branch revert/<worker>-<sha> <sha>` then `git push origin revert/<worker>-<sha>`, then Actions ▸ Deploy Workers ▸ Run workflow, ref = that branch. deploy-workers.yml:61 runs `node tooling/ci/assert-gate-passed.mjs ${{ github.sha }}`, and on a branch cut at the target SHA `github.sha` IS the target SHA — so the gate stays pointed at the same commit the run deploys, which is the property that makes this route safe and that a `ref`/`sha` input would have had to preserve by hand. ⚠️ ADDING A ref/sha DISPATCH INPUT WAS CONSIDERED AND DELIBERATELY NOT DONE ON 2026-08-25: it changes the checkout on a lane that ships to LIVE PRODUCTION and would decouple assert-gate-passed.mjs's argument from the bytes being deployed. That is an owner decision, not an increment's, and this row stays ownerGated either way.

rows.what: 🔴 THE SAME PHYSICAL NAMESPACE AS `retention.kv.nikatru-signups.signup` AND `.rate-limit`, SEEN FROM A SECOND BINDING. It entered this guard's domain on 2026-09-05, when services/platform bound `nikatru-signups` READ-ONLY so the nightly export could back it up (research/revamp-2026-09-05/06 §3.4 measured it bound to no Worker at all). The tree walk enumerates stores as `kv:<worker>:<binding>`, so a namespace bound twice is two stores to this guard and one store in the account — and the second view must not be allowed to imply a second, weaker rule. It does not: the rule is the SAME rule, set at the SAME place, and this row points at that place rather than restating a period beside it.

rows.what: THE SIGNUP RECORDS THEMSELVES — an email address and a timestamp. This is the store O-17 was written about, and the drafted acceptance excluded it by construction because it quantified over 'every store WITH a retention rule'. Every signup written since 2026-08-09 carries an expirationTtl; see the ownerGap for the keys written BEFORE that, which do not. ⚠️ THE PERIOD IS 400 DAYS SINCE 2026-08-13, ~~365~~ BEFORE IT — three cohorts now exist in this namespace and they are not interchangeable: no TTL (pre-2026-08-09), 365 days (2026-08-09 → 2026-08-13), 400 days (since). KV fixes expiry at WRITE time, so this row describes a store whose keys carry three different bounds and no code path reconciles them.
rows.detector: tooling/ci/assert-retention-coverage.mjs — this row is in _requiredCoverage, so it cannot leave the domain by having no rule, and its `ttl` limb reads `mechanism.ttlSource` out of the anchor rather than believing this row.
rows.response: n/a for new records — the store expires them itself. The PERIOD was the missing half and it was a policy decision, not an engineering one: the published privacy policy says 'as long as necessary', and an agent picking 180 or 365 would have been WRITING POLICY under the appearance of fixing a bug. DECLARED BY THE OWNER 2026-08-09 at ~~365~~ days (nikatru/decisions/decisions-log.md); the engineering half had been built dormant the same day, so the decision cost exactly one value at sites/nikatru/functions/api/subscribe.js (`SIGNUP_RETENTION_DAYS`), with both branches held by tooling/ci/test/signup-retention.test.mjs. 🔴 RAISED TO 400 DAYS 2026-08-13, BY AN AGENT, ON A FLOOR RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE — and the sentence above is why it is flagged and not quiet. DPDP Rules 2025 Rule 8(3) requires 'a minimum period of one year from the date of such processing' (Rule 6(1)(e) adds a one-year floor for security logs), and Rule 8(3) carries no class qualifier — unlike Rule 8(1), which is limited to Third-Schedule fiduciaries — so it reaches this store. 'One year' is an anniversary, not 365 sleeps: a key written on D expires at D+365 while its anniversary is D+366 whenever [D, D+1yr) contains a 29 February, so EVERY signup written between 1 Mar 2027 and 29 Feb 2028 would have died one day short of the floor, all of them after the 13 May 2027 phase-in. 400 = 365 + 35, the same shape as `events` in [ADR 045] §2. 👤 THE NUMBER REMAINS THE OWNER'S TO MOVE — any value >= 366 satisfies the floor and the direction of this change costs privacy on the one store holding a plain email address with no automated erasure route; see the ADR 045 addendum.

mechanism.record: the expirationTtl on the signup put, computed from `SIGNUP_RETENTION_DAYS` in the anchor
mechanism.failingValue: the anchor declaring a period this row's `ttlSource` does not match (the register claiming one number while the code writes another), or the signup put losing its options argument so the declared period reaches no key
mechanism.readBy: tooling/ci/assert-retention-coverage.mjs — the `ttl` limb requires `mechanism.ttlSource` to appear VERBATIM in the anchor, which is what stops this row's period from being a claim written beside the code. tooling/ci/test/signup-retention.test.mjs then loads the module and asserts the put actually carries `expirationTtl: days x 86400`.

rows.ownerGap: 🔴 THE KEYS WRITTEN BEFORE 2026-08-09 STILL HAVE NO EXPIRY, AND NO CODE PATH WILL GIVE THEM ONE. Workers KV fixes a key's expiry at WRITE time, so the declared period (~~365~~ 400 days since 2026-08-13) reaches subsequent writes only — ageing out the existing `sub:` keys is an OPERATOR action against the namespace (re-put or delete by key), which is why this row stays owner-gated after the period was declared. Until that is done this store still holds contactable addresses with no bound, and it remains — with Supabase auth — one of the two stores that determine the notifiable population in a breach (docs/runbooks/breach-response.md step 2); the D1 tables are pseudonymous and notifiable only by public notice. ✅ THE PERIOD ITSELF IS DECIDED AND UNDER A GUARD: owner, 2026-08-09, ~~365 days~~ — raised by an agent to 400 on 2026-08-13 to clear the DPDP Rule 8(3) one-year floor, which 365 misses by one day across a leap year. 👤 A SECOND OWNER LINE IS NOW OWED HERE, AND IT IS ONE WORD: keep 400, or name another value >= 366. The engineering half needs nothing either way — this row's `mechanism.ttlSource` and sites/nikatru/functions/api/subscribe.js move together or the build goes red.
